name: Hearth
title: Every qualified contractor lead gets a useful next step
subtitle: Inbound conversion · Lead routing · Contractor activation
focus: Find the right contractor, route the lead quickly and measure whether the handoff produces activation and retention.
priorities: Build and own the inbound conversion engine.
Improve qualification, routing and next-best actions.
Connect Salesforce / HubSpot, Redshift, Clay and AI-assisted workflows.
Measure business outcomes with experiments and causal discipline.
layers: Lead source, trade, service area and requested workflow.
Contractor fit and a verified contact; keep uncertain fields in review.
Available owner, clear SLA and an actionable next step.
Meetings held, activation and retention by cohort and experiment assignment.
rules: Financing interest is not proof of borrower eligibility or approval.
Respect existing account ownership and contact history.
A faster response is a testable intervention, not proof of causal lift.

actions.title: Recover the unfinished booking
actions.detail: Inspect lead → owner → response → meeting so the next step is explicit.

actions.title: Route by trade and service area
actions.detail: Send the contractor to the right owner with the original request attached.

actions.title: Check first-workflow activation
actions.detail: Find the missing step after onboarding instead of sending a generic reminder.

actions.title: Audit response receipts
actions.detail: A delivered message is different from a reply or held meeting.

actions.title: Keep the holdout intact
actions.detail: Compare like-for-like lead cohorts before attributing a conversion change.

actions.title: Inspect duplicate acquisition

personas.name: Contractor owner
personas.pain: A customer conversation interrupted by complicated financing and follow-through
personas.promise: A trade-relevant conversation about the sales workflow the owner wants to improve.
personas.subject: A useful next step for {{trade}} projects
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, you asked about {{requested_workflow}} for your {{trade}} business. What happens today between the first customer quote and the next decision? I’d like to understand that handoff before suggesting a workflow.
personas.question: Which part of your quote-to-customer process causes the most follow-up?

personas.name: Sales / office manager
personas.pain: Leads and customer tasks without clear ownership
personas.promise: A clear next step, an owner and a visible follow-up receipt.
personas.subject: Following up on {{business}}’s request
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, I’m following up on the request about {{requested_workflow}}. Would it be more useful to review the current process together, or first answer one specific question? I can keep the next step focused on how your team works.
personas.question: Who should own the next step, and what would make a short conversation useful?

pitch: I am a founder who has shipped a revenue-generating iOS app and built inquiry, matching, billing and follow-up workflows. I also bring years of outbound sales and closing experience. At Hearth, I would connect that builder-operator perspective to the contractor lead journey: the right fit, a clear owner, a useful next step and measurement through activation.
mappings: Hire Line Dancers: matching, private inquiries and follow-up recovery.
Make the lead-to-next-step workflow complete and observable.
Shipped product onboarding and PostHog funnel work.
Define one activation event and test the intervention against a baseline.
Founder experience plus startup positioning, outbound and closing.
Build a small usable workflow, observe sellers and iterate on outcomes.
northStar: Qualified contractors who activate and keep using the product
weekOne: A complete lead-to-owner-to-next-step workflow for one contractor source.
days60: Improve the first-workflow activation journey and compare trade-specific cohorts with a documented baseline.
days90: Scale the strongest intervention using activation and retention outcomes, with causal limits and operational cost visible.

competitors.name: Wisetack
competitors.context: Offers customer financing for real-life service businesses.
competitors.question: Is the contractor primarily solving homeowner payment flexibility, lead response, or the broader quote-to-payment workflow? Compare the relevant financing terms directly before making claims.

competitors.name: Jobber
competitors.context: Offers software for service-business quotes, scheduling, work and payments.
competitors.question: Which contractor workflows already work in the existing system, and what acquisition, call handling or financing gap is still worth solving? Treat overlap as partial rather than identical.

firstBuilds.title: Inbound handoff recovery
firstBuilds.goal: Make the step after a qualified form submission dependable.
firstBuilds.scope: 50 historical inbound leads and one reviewed live source.
firstBuilds.measure: Owner accuracy, response receipts, held meetings and booking dropoff.

firstBuilds.title: Trade-aware qualification
firstBuilds.goal: Keep the conversation relevant to the contractor’s business.
firstBuilds.scope: One trade cohort with a documented manual baseline.
firstBuilds.measure: Qualified-lead agreement, missing fields and useful owner context.

firstBuilds.title: Activation experiment
firstBuilds.goal: Test one intervention with a clear outcome and comparison group.
firstBuilds.scope: A narrow activation milestone with an agreed holdout.
firstBuilds.measure: Activation, retention, intervention cost and cohort balance.

projectRelevance.sammy: Structured source data, deduplication and validation are useful for clean contractor qualification and service-area context.
projectRelevance.sidequest: Onboarding, analytics and a local partnership CRM connect acquisition, activation and commercial feedback.
projectRelevance.dancers: Matching by service area, private inquiries and durable follow-up closely relate to contractor lead handoffs and recovery.
